+
+    `Exchange.ManageV2` and `Exchange.ManageAsAppV2` permissions are being retired. Use `Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage` for delegated access and `Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp` for app-only access. englishSummary.headline: Admin API permissions are changing
englishSummary.summary: The documentation states that Exchange.ManageV2 and Exchange.ManageAsAppV2 are being retired and replaces them with Exchange.AdminAPI.Manage and Exchange.AdminAPI.ManageAsApp. It also says the described features are now generally available.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Update delegated and app-only application permissions, consent, and token configuration to use the new permission names.

+++ b/Exchange/ExchangeOnline/reference/admin-api-overview.md
@@ -56,7 +56,7 @@ platformId: 1c7043d0-461f-1410-762c-8614c61048d1
 
 Note
 
-The features described in this article are currently in Preview, aren't available in all organizations, and are subject to change.
+The features described in this article are now generally available to all organizations.
 
 The Exchange Online Admin API is a REST-based administrative surface that enables a focused set of Exchange cmdlets and parameters as POST-only endpoints. The API enables access to a few key tasks that were previously available through Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is [planned for deprecation in October 2026](../clients-and-mobile-in-exchange-online/deprecation-of-ews-exchange-online). The API is built for these specific scenarios and *doesn't* replace the full Exchange administration surface in Exchange Online PowerShell.

englishSummary.headline: Exchange Admin API features are available to all organizations
englishSummary.summary: The documentation states that the features are now generally available to all organizations.
englishSummary.adminImpact: Administrators can use the documented features across all organizations; no action is specified.
